title: Course Schedule
notes:
Task: Given numCourses and prerequisite pairs [a,b] meaning b must precede a, return whether all courses can be completed. Example: numCourses=2, prerequisites=[[1,0]] -> true.
Idea: Build prerequisite edges and count incoming edges. Kahn's algorithm processes zero-indegree courses; a cycle leaves at least one course unprocessed.
Invariant: The processed prefix/range maintains the information needed to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty inputs, singleton inputs, and boundary conditions are handled where permitted.
complexity_reason: Build prerequisite edges and count incoming edges. Kahn's algorithm processes zero-indegree courses; a cycle leaves at least one course unprocessed.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
notes:

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
notes:
Task: Given positive integers nums and target, return the minimum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target, or 0 if none exists. Example: target=7, nums=[2,3,1,2,4,3] -> 2.
Idea: Expand the right edge to reach the target, then shrink from the left while the window remains valid to find the shortest valid window.
Invariant: The processed prefix/range maintains the information needed to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty inputs, singleton inputs, and boundary conditions are handled where permitted.
complexity_reason: Expand the right edge to reach the target, then shrink from the left while the window remains valid to find the shortest valid window.

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
notes:
Task: Design WordDictionary with addWord(word) and search(word), where '.' matches any single letter.
Idea: Store words in a trie. For a literal character follow one child; for '.' recursively try every existing child at that depth.
Invariant: The processed prefix/range maintains the information needed to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty inputs, singleton inputs, and boundary conditions are handled where permitted.
time_complexity: Add O(L); search O(26^L) worst case
complexity_reason: Store words in a trie. For a literal character follow one child; for '.' recursively try every existing child at that depth.

title: House Robber II
notes:
Task: Houses are arranged in a circle, so the first and last houses are adjacent. Return the maximum amount without robbing adjacent houses. Example: [2,3,2] -> 3.
Idea: For more than one house, exclude the first or exclude the last; each remaining range is a linear House Robber problem.
Invariant: The processed prefix/range maintains the information needed to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty inputs, singleton inputs, and boundary conditions are handled where permitted.
complexity_reason: For more than one house, exclude the first or exclude the last; each remaining range is a linear House Robber problem.

title: Invert Binary Tree
notes:
Task: Invert a binary tree by swapping each node's left and right children. Example: root [4,2,7,1,3,6,9] becomes [4,7,2,9,6,3,1].
Idea: Recursively invert both subtrees and swap their positions. Every node is visited once.
Invariant: The processed prefix/range maintains the information needed to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty inputs, singleton inputs, and boundary conditions are handled where permitted.
complexity_reason: Recursively invert both subtrees and swap their positions. Every node is visited once.

title: Summary Ranges
notes:
Task: Given a sorted unique integer array, summarize consecutive runs as 'start->end' and singletons as 'start'. Example: [0,1,2,4,5,7] -> ['0->2','4->5','7'].
Idea: Start a range at each unprocessed number and advance while the next number is exactly one greater. Emit either a singleton or an inclusive range.
Invariant: The processed prefix/range maintains the information needed to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty inputs, singleton inputs, and boundary conditions are handled where permitted.
complexity_reason: Start a range at each unprocessed number and advance while the next number is exactly one greater. Emit either a singleton or an inclusive range.

title: Power of Two
notes:
Task: Return true if n is a positive power of two. Example: 16 -> true; 3 -> false.
Idea: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit. Subtracting one clears that bit and sets all lower bits, so n & (n-1) is zero.
Invariant: The processed prefix/range maintains the information needed to make the next decision correctly.
Edge cases: Empty inputs, singleton inputs, and boundary conditions are handled where permitted.
complexity_reason: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit. Subtracting one clears that bit and sets all lower bits, so n & (n-1) is zero.
